title: if/else among the tools you know
idea: Mix if/else with comparisons, booleans, variables, and math from earlier units. Spaced review alongside the new tool.

exercises.prompt:
Review of Unit 20: what will this show?

print(9 <= 9)
exercises.explanation: 9 equals 9, and <= accepts equal, so True. Comparisons still return booleans.

exercises.prompt: Review of Unit 19: what kind of value is False?
exercises.explanation: False is a boolean — the yes/no kind of value that drives an if/else.
is_open is True, so the if branch runs: Come in. A boolean variable works as the condition on its own.

exercises.prompt:
Review of earlier math: what will this show?

total = 3 * 4
print(total)
exercises.explanation: 3 * 4 is 12, stored in total and printed. Arithmetic still works just as before.
items * 2 is 12, then 12 >= 10 is True, so Enough prints.

exercises.prompt: Review the = vs == trap. Which if condition is correct?
exercises.explanation: A condition checks, so ==. 'One store, two ask' still holds inside an if/else.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show, line by line?

score = 55
if score >= 60:
    print("Pass")
else:
    print("Fail")
print("Thanks")
exercises.explanation: 55 >= 60 is False, so else runs: Fail. The un-indented Thanks always runs. Output: Fail, then Thanks.

exercises.prompt: Match each value to its kind (a mixed review).
exercises.explanation: Digits are numbers, quotes mark text, True/False are booleans. Booleans are what an if/else acts on.

exercises.prompt:
Review of Unit 15: what will this show?

name = "Sam"
print("Hi " + name)
exercises.explanation: Joining text with + gives "Hi Sam". Strings and + still work as they did in the earlier unit.

exercises.prompt: What does this review lesson show about if/else?
options: It works together with comparisons, booleans, variables, and math you already know
It replaces all the earlier tools
It cannot use a boolean variable
exercises.explanation: if/else sits on top of everything so far: a comparison or boolean picks the branch, and each branch uses your existing tools.
